overview: Oilfield Chemicals Demand Forecasting addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in oil, gas and petrochemicals operations. The first proof of value uses chemical injection rates, tank levels and delivery lead times. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is critical chemical shortage events, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: chemical injection rates, tank levels and delivery lead times; define critical chemical shortage events and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Asset Integrity Director / Production Manager.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
